# Styles


---

## The digital page, so far

- no fixed dimension
  
- light or no table of contents/hierarchy

- basic tags control appearance

- tag names and their effects are part of the HTML5 industrial standard 

- minor variations on how browsers render HTML formatting.


---

## Style personalization

inside each tag we can re-assign some style measures, e.g., colour:

```html
<tag style="attribute:value;">my text</tag>
```

Both ``attribute`` and ``value`` must be selected from a list of admitted names/values.

Mind the syntax: ``style``, ``=``, ``""``, ``:`` and ``;`` are all indespensible.

---

## Examples

```html
<strong style="color: red;">Lorem Ipsum<strong>
```

- try it on your project

```html
<strong style="color: red; font-weight: bolder;">Lorem Ipsum</strong>
```

(check fonts weights on [Mozilla](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/font-weight))

---

but what about

```html
<b>L</b>orem ipsum <strong style="color: red;">dolor</strong> sit amet, consectetur 
```

<b>L</b>orem ipsum <strong style="color: red;">dolor</strong> sit amet, consectetur 

- too muany visuals at once

- the source quickly becomes unreadable

- hard to make global changes (e.g., all instances of *dolor* now become green)

---

## A special operation

```html
<div style=”text-indent: 16px;”>
```

## Digital twins

A new concept in Engineering

From [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digital_twin):

*[...] a computational model of an intended or actual real-world physical product, system, or process (a physical twin)* 

. . .

*that serves as a digital counterpart of it for purposes such as simulation, integration, testing, monitoring, and maintenance.*

---

## Digital twins


*[...] a computational model of an intended or actual real-world physical product, system, or process (a physical twin) that serves as a digital counterpart of it for purposes such as simulation, integration, testing, monitoring, and maintenance.*

. . .

*By its strict definition, a digital twin is distinguished from an ordinary simulation in that it continuously uses real data from its physical counterpart to dynamically synchronize with the real system.*

# Styling pages


---

## Idea

- redefine tags with our styles

- create new tags to attach specific styles to text

- __keep webpage styles separated from content__

---

## The engineering of styles

- styles change seldom, mostly through large *facelifting* operations, graphics experts work on them

- contents may change by the minute and are produced by a variety of actors (journalists)

- to keep consistency across large web sites and re-use styles, two or more CSS files could be applied to one page


# The CSS standard

---

![](https://kinsta.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/08/html-vs-css.png)


---
 
## Catch-up work 

(discretionary for those who already used ``mystyle.css``)  

from VS Code create a new CSS file, e.g., ``mystyle.css`` and save it alongside your Lorem ipsum page

write on it: 

  ```css
  p {
      text-indent: 20px;
      text-align: justify;
      letter-spacing: 3px;
    }

  span {
        background-color: yellow;
      } 
  ```

Notice the different syntax; use the embedded *code selector*

---


## Linking up your style


```html
  <link href="mystyle.css" rel="stylesheet" type="text/css" />
```  

reload to see how the browser applies the definitions from ``mystyle.css`` to the tags.

Linking is *syntactical:* href value should be a valid path inside your folders

- ``  href="./mystyle.css"``  in the same folder

- ``  href="../mystyle.css"``  in the folder above


---

## Where's my style?

- ``href="../../mystyle.css"``  two folders above

- ``href="../30-visuals/mystyle.css"``  in the *sibling/parallel* folder called ``30-visuals``

Always check by following up links

---

## Change the mood, all at once

```css
body {
	font: 11px georgia, serif;
	text-align: center;
	color: #fff;
	background: #748A9B;
	margin: 0px;
	}
```

Put this, the least-specific definition, as first in the CSS file


---

This should be the default

```css
h1, h2 {
        text-align: center;
        }
```

```css
h1 {
    color: purple;
    }
```
